root_cause_diagnosis.detailed_explanation: 1. Calibration Offset: The pre-frozen Isotonic Calibrator shifts model predictions up to mean 0.1666, which is more than 2x the true dataset prevalence of 0.0802. This calibration bias alone adds ~0.0075 to the Brier score, driving BSS deeply negative (-0.5405). 2. Fixture Noise: In the synthetic fixture generation, shock bust events were generated with uniform random probability uncorrelated with ensemble spread features, limiting discriminative AUC to ~0.526. 3. Remedy: Recalibration on an out-of-time validation split restores mean calibration to match base rate, and training-time baseline freezing ensures honest BSS calculation.
